requirements: #164 real-process Host SIGKILL, restart reconciliation, replay, truth, and retained evidence
environmentAndTransport: npm-packed Sand-King installed outside the checkout on Linux x64/arm64
real npm-pinned headless Chromium Cockpit over authenticated loopback WebSocket
real Controller runtime and framed local Host with Host-private state
pinned deterministic conformance Harness adapter supervised through the native process-tree guardian
initialState: one ordinary Git Project with a pinned reusable Harness registration
no Harness run, launch lookup, or Sand-King Project file
one clean Controller runtime and Host identity binding
actionsAndFaultPoints: launch through the ordinary Controller CLI visible in the packaged Cockpit
wait for durable run identity, immutable execution snapshot, readiness, events, and diagnostic ranges
SIGKILL the real Host at real_host_sigkill_after_active_publication
restart from the same private state and reopen the packaged Cockpit
retry the original launch hash and then launch deliberately with a fresh key
expectedTypedResults: harness_run_created followed by one failed/incomplete host_daemon_interrupted outcome
same-key launch returns the original run identity as an idempotent replay
fresh-key launch creates a distinct run without rewriting the interrupted run
canonicalInvariants: one immutable run identity and execution snapshot survive Host death
ordered earlier events and diagnostic range references survive restart
one terminal event and outcome agree with the current Cockpit view
the original adapter process tree terminates and is never relaunched automatically
prohibitedSideEffects: invented success
duplicate run, adapter start, terminal event, or accepted audit
raw retry key, credential, environment dump, process handle, or numeric process target disclosure
Project write or tracked Sand-King file

requirements: #164 cancellation acceptance, signalling, termination, restart, and replay boundaries
environmentAndTransport: npm-packed Sand-King and packaged loopback Cockpit
real Controller runtime, framed local Host, deterministic Harness, and complete-tree process guardian
initialState: one active deterministic Harness run with readiness and diagnostics durably observable
no terminal outcome and no prior cancellation lookup
actionsAndFaultPoints: accept cancellation through the Cockpit
interrupt before signalling, after cooperative or forced signalling, and while awaiting termination
SIGKILL and restart the Host after durable cancellation acceptance
retry the same cancellation-key hash
expectedTypedResults: restart converges once to cancelled after confirmed termination or recovery_required when unproved
same-key cancellation replays the original typed acceptance without another signal
canonicalInvariants: accepted cancellation survives browser, Controller, and Host interruption
no Harness-defined progress is accepted after cancellation
cancelled is published only after complete-tree termination proof
prohibitedSideEffects: second cancellation transition or signal
invented cancelled result under uncertain termination
replacement Harness work
Project write, raw key, process handle, or environment disclosure

requirements: #164 state and race coverage for completion on both sides of cancellation acceptance
environmentAndTransport: Host-private deterministic component fixture using the real conformance Harness process
typed Controller-to-Host launch, cancellation, observation, and outcome contracts
initialState: one active run at the serialized terminal/cancellation arbitration boundary
one valid structured terminal envelope and one fresh cancellation key
actionsAndFaultPoints: pause immediately before terminal-envelope/outcome commit and accept cancellation first
commit a valid terminal result first and submit cancellation second
observe ordered history and retained audits after each interleaving
expectedTypedResults: a valid terminal result accepted first remains succeeded or failed
cancellation accepted first follows bounded cancellation and becomes cancelled only after termination
later cancellation against a terminal run returns harness_run_not_cancellable
canonicalInvariants: one terminal event and structured outcome
current status, event history, envelope validation, and audits agree
prohibitedSideEffects: contradictory succeeded and cancelled outcomes
two terminal events
success inferred from logs or exit
caller-visible entity-revision precondition

requirements: #164 bounded public recovery, replay, security, and retained process-fact evidence
environmentAndTransport: npm-packed Sand-King and packaged loopback Cockpit
real Controller runtime and Host restart over Host-private recovery state
initialState: one interrupted run whose related process state cannot initially be proved terminated
no accepted terminal envelope and no replacement run
actionsAndFaultPoints: restart into recovery_required
inspect sanitized process facts and bounded actions through the Cockpit
recheck with a hashed retry key, reconnect, and replay the original action
finalize only after termination becomes confirmed
expectedTypedResults: harness_process_termination_unconfirmed with recheck and only identity-safe actions
one failed/incomplete host_daemon_interrupted outcome after confirmed finalization
canonicalInvariants: current process observation may advance without rewriting detection history
an unrelated or PID-reused process is never adopted or targeted
recovery never launches replacement Harness work
prohibitedSideEffects: invented success, failure, or cancellation before proof
unrestricted process API, handle, PID, command, or environment disclosure
duplicate destructive action or terminal result
Project write

requirements: #164 deterministic fault, protocol, state, security, and packaged-browser merge gate
environmentAndTransport: test-only deterministic fault callback instrumented only into a temporary npm-packed Host copy
packaged loopback Cockpit through the authenticated browser, Controller-runtime, and framed local-Host boundaries
supported Linux, Windows, and macOS process supervision suites
initialState: fresh, active, cancelling, recovery_required, and terminal state fixtures
bounded raw key, credential, environment, process, and Project-change security markers
actionsAndFaultPoints: interrupt immediately before and after every faultMatrix publication or action point
restart repeatedly from the exact retained Host-private bytes
retry launch, cancellation, and recovery with matching and conflicting request fingerprints
refresh/reconnect observation cursors
expectedTypedResults: pre-commit faults leave no claimed accepted effect
post-commit faults preserve exact keyed replay and repair only missing audits or current view
typed terminal, recovery, resync-required, conflict, and unsupported-platform results remain schema-valid
canonicalInvariants: immutable snapshot and ordered event history agree with the current view
acknowledged effects survive and unacknowledged effects are never claimed
keyed mutations, terminal outcomes, signals, and recovery actions do not duplicate
no operation accepts an expected Harness-run entity revision
prohibitedSideEffects: production CLI, Host, protocol, or browser fault-control API
invented success or duplicate canonical mutation
credential, raw retry key, environment dump, unrestricted process handle, or tracked Project change in any public or retained surface
Project or Harness-workspace execution-state file
